summary:
This project is an interactive, Sci-fi-inspired game that introduces players to the challenges of designing space missions. Players take the role of mission designers, assembling spacecraft, choosing scientific instruments, communication systems, power sources, and launch vehicles while balancing limited budgets, mass, and energy resources.
The project transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. Through mission planning, resource management, and spaceflight simulation, players discover how engineering decisions influence mission performance.
By combining gaming and scientific concepts,Mission to the Stars makes space exploration more attractive and inspires players to develop an interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematical calculations.
details:
1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

“Orbital Commander” is an interactive, browser-based game that gives players the opportunity to experience the challenges of designing and managing a space mission. It addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge, Space Mission Design Game, by transforming the complex process of mission planning into an accessible and engaging simulation.

Players begin by selecting a mission objective, such as planetary exploration, off-world agriculture, or randomly generated mission. They then design their spacecraft by selecting essential components, including launch vehicles, spacecraft systems, scientific instruments, communication equipment, and power sources.

Every decision involves trade-offs. Players must balance spacecraft mass, budget, energy, and mission requirements to create a viable spacecraft.

2. What benefits does it have?

The main benefit is that it makes aerospace engineering and space science easier to understand through practical experimentation.

Players can:

  • Understand the basic stages involved in planning a space mission.
  • Practise managing limited resources such as money, energy, and spacecraft mass.
  • Understand how engineering decisions influence the outcome of a mission.

The game also provides an opportunity to learn through experimentation: players can try different spacecraft configurations, compare their choices, and discover why some mission designs are more effective than others.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our objective is to make space exploration and aerospace engineering more accessible, especially to the people who may not have previous experience with these subjects.

We want to inspire curiosity about the universe and encourage interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). By allowing players to experience the decisions involved in a space mission, the project helps connect scientific theory with practical applications.

In the longer term, we plan to demonstrate that space exploration is not only about launching rockets: it also requires scientific research, engineering, teamwork, planning, and responsible use of resources.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

The project is developed as a browser-based application by Bolt.New AI tool and is hosted through the Bolt platform.

Its intended technical approach includes:

  • Development platform: Bolt for creating and developing the web application.
  • Web technologies: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and other technologies.
  • Simulation: Mathematical models and calculations representing orbital motion and gravitational interactions.
  • Deployment: Web hosting through the Bolt hosting platform.
  • Hardware: A standard computer, laptop, tablet, or other device capable of running a modern web browser.

5. How is the project creative?

The creative aspect of Mission to the Stars is its combination of education, simulation, and game-based exploration.

Instead of simply showing how a spacecraft works, the game puts the player in the role of a mission designer. Players are encouraged to experiment, make engineering decisions, manage resources, and discover the consequences of their choices.

The project uses a science-fiction-inspired visual style to make the experience immersive and exciting. Its different mission scenarios encourage exploration beyond a single destination or objective. The spacecraft-building process also gives players a sense of ownership over their missions: each design can lead to a different outcome.

By combining real scientific principles with interactive gameplay, the project makes complex aerospace concepts more approachable without losing sight of the engineering challenges behind actual space exploration.

6. What factors did the team consider?

Several important factors influenced the project design:

  • Mission objectives: Different missions require different spacecraft configurations, equipment, and scientific capabilities.
  • Engineering trade-offs: Players must consider the relationship between spacecraft mass, power, budget, communications, and mission performance.
  • Resource management: Limited energy and financial resources make planning and prioritisation important.
  • Educational accessibility: The game should be understandable and enjoyable for people without advanced scientific or engineering knowledge.
  • User experience: The interface should make mission planning and simulation intuitive and engaging.
  • Creativity and experimentation: Players should be able to explore different strategies and learn from the results.
  • Technical feasibility: The project should work as a browser-based experience without requiring specialised hardware.
  • Inspiration and engagement: The visual design and gameplay should encourage curiosity about space and future exploration.

Conclusion

Mission to the Stars transforms the complex process of designing a space mission into an interactive educational adventure. By combining spacecraft construction, resource management, scientific concepts, and space simulation, it gives players an opportunity to think like real mission designers. Our goal is to make aerospace engineering more accessible, encourage STEM learning, and inspire the next generation to explore the possibilities of space.
